entries.name: Astrakhan town mark
entries.looks_like: A crown above a curved sword, in a rectangle.
entries.means: Assayed in Astrakhan.
entries.date_note: Rosenberg: Beschauzeichen 1771. Rosenberg's spelling: Astrachan. Postnikova-Loseva: the arms of Astrakhan, a crown and a sword, used from the second half of the 18th century to 1884.

entries.name: Irkutsk or Tobolsk town mark
entries.looks_like: Two upright animals facing each other under a crown, in a rectangle.
entries.means: Assayed in Tobolsk (1765–1780) or Irkutsk (1777–1799); the Irkutsk mark adds the letters ГИ.
entries.date_note: Rosenberg: Beschauzeichen 1774, 1776. Rosenberg's spelling: Irkutsk oder Tobolsk. Postnikova-Loseva: the arms of Siberia, two sables holding a bow and arrows under a crown, were struck in Tobolsk 1765–1780 and, with the letters ГИ, in Irkutsk 1777–1799. So both readings are right; Irkutsk marks carry ГИ.

visual.credit: Facsimile from Marc Rosenberg, Der Goldschmiede Merkzeichen, 3rd ed., vol. 4 (1928), p. 465, public domain.

entries.means: Assayed in Yaroslavl.
entries.date_note: Rosenberg: Beschauzeichen 1756, 1767. Rosenberg's spelling: Jarosslawl. Postnikova-Loseva: a bear standing on its hind legs holding an axe, from the second quarter of the 18th century to 1885; nos. 3787–3788 are dated 1755–1760 and 1761–1770.

entries.name: Kaluga town mark
entries.looks_like: A shield with a small crown above wavy lines of water.
entries.means: Assayed in Kaluga.
entries.date_note: Rosenberg: Beschauzeichen 1797, 1799. Rosenberg's spelling: Kaluga. Postnikova-Loseva: the arms approved in 1777, an imperial crown over two wavy lines for the river Oka; no. 516 is dated end of the 18th to early 19th century. The earliest Kaluga mark (1772–1786) was a double-headed eagle with ГК.

visual.credit: Facsimile from Marc Rosenberg, Der Goldschmiede Merkzeichen, 3rd ed., vol. 4 (1928), p. 465, public domain.
